currentContext.expansion: MMTC has no expansion programme. The Company has undertaken no business activity since April 2022 in pursuance of the direction of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, and continues on a non-operating basis pending a formal Government decision on closure. Its only physical asset in operation is a 15 MW Wind Mill project with 25 Wind Energy Generators, set up in March 2007 at Gajendragad in Karnataka at a total cost of approximately Rs. 68.5 crores on 31 acres of land leased from the Karnataka State Government for 30 years; power is sold to Hubli Electricity Company Limited (HESCOM) under a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement signed in July 2007. That PPA expires in March 2027, and the Company is exploring possibilities for running the project for another 5-10 years and making efforts to obtain approval for its renewal. Elsewhere the direction is contraction rather than expansion: the Singapore subsidiary MMTC Transnational Pte Ltd is in liquidation, the Sical Iron Ore Terminal JV is under NCLT liquidation, the Kandla land was surrendered in 2020 with a winding-up application for Kandla Free Trade Warehousing pending before the NCLT, and the Haldia land was surrendered to the Haldia Development Authority. The Company is instead seeking cost reduction and income from renting out surplus office space.
